notes.title: Release: Text & Copy Between Scenes
notes.content:
[H1]Text Input[/H1]
Definitely our most requested feature, you can now add text to any scene. Text will behave exactly like any other object, which means it can be snapped, resized and grouped.

[H1]Comfort Mode[/H1]
For our users that are susceptible to motion sickness, we've added comfort mode, which applies an FOV limiting effect when moving around the scene, much like in Google Earth. It is off by default and can be turned on from settings.

[H1]Copy and Paste Between Scenes[/H1]
You can now copy an object to the clipboard, and paste that object between scenes. It's really useful if you've added an object to a scene and want that object to appear in many other scenes. See the video below for more information.

[H1]Other Improvements[/H1]
>Ability to move the scene while holding an object (in general most interactions are now possible while moving the scene, even drawing)
>Left/right handedness and comfort mode settings are saved between sessions
>Expanded keyboard to include punctuation and shift/caps functionality
>General performance/rendering improvements
>Lots of minor bug fixes 🐛

Read more here: https://blog.sketchbox3d.com/release-text-copy-between-scenes-f66b7b076234

notes.title: Release: Scale for Models
notes.content:
Over the last two weeks we focused on scale. And I’m excited to announce that you can now import models with the correct scale and see the dimensions of a model.

[h1]Import Models with Scale[/h1]
When importing a model into Sketchbox (GLTF, OBJ or FBX) Sketchbox will read the model file, and import the model with whatever units were in the file (mm, cm, m, km, in or ft). Using ‘Model Settings’ you can change the units of any model.


[h1]Reset Scale & Position[/h1]
The absolute size of the model (eg. 3m x 4m x 1m) is displayed in the ‘Model Settings’ panel. ‘Reset Position’ will move the model to the origin. ‘Reset Scale’ will reset the scale of the model (eg. 1x1x1)


[h1]Size Indicators[/h1]
The absolute size of every model is now shown when you resize the model, or when you hover on one of the control points.


[h1]Unit Settings for Projects[/h1]
Every project now has a unit setting, and can be switched between meters and feet.

notes.title: Major Release: Snapping V2 + FBX Import + WindowsMR Support
notes.content:
I’m really excited to announce this release, we’ve spent the last few weeks improving our snapping system and it’s the biggest improvement since we added Poly.


[h1]  Snap to Normal & Preview Snap Location [/h1] 
Before, it was unclear where an object would snap to, and each object only had one plane that other objects could be snapped to. See example below.

With snapping to the normal, you can easily snap objects to larger objects and quickly build rooms/scenes. And it just feels right. In the example below, we can easily snap a bookshelf to a wall that’s part of the ‘bedroom’ object.

[h1]  Snap to any side of an Object [/h1] 
Before it was only possible to snap to a single side of any object (the origin plane). Objects now have bounding boxes and you can snap to any side of the bounding box.

[h1]  Rename Projects [/h1] 
You can now rename projects by opening Settings and pressing ‘rename’. The name you choose will show up on the homescreen, and in windows explorer.

[h1] Toggle Snapping On/Off [/h1] 
Sometimes, you really don’t want objects to snap together. Like in the example below, if you want to place tools loosely into a tool case. Snapping is ON by default and can be toggled OFF by HOLDING down the A button.

[h1]  FBX Import [/h1] 
You’ve been requesting FBX import since we first released Sketchbox, and it’s finally here! We’ve tested it with FBX files generated by all the major 3D desktop tools, and lots more that we found on Sketchfab.

If you find an FBX file that doesn’t import properly, please email us.

[h1] Windows MR Support [/h1] 
Sketchbox now supports all Windows MR headsets via the SteamVR adapter.

[h1] Project Renaming [/h1] 
The new project renaming feature makes it easier to keep all your projects organized.


[h1] Coming Soon: Sketchfab Integration [/h1] 
Last week Sketchfab announced their Download API. We’ve been working with them to make their library of over 100,000 models instantly accessible in Sketchbox. We’re super excited about this but it isn’t quite ready for release.

[h1] Other Improvements [/h1] 
* After importing a model or image, we now automatically switch to the select tool so you can position it
* When switching between scene viewpoints you’re now more likely to be looking in the intended direction
* FBX export look better when imported into Unity
* You can now search across all models on Google poly (high poly and low poly). High poly models will take longer to download. 🔺
* Menu disappears during select
* Poly color will work in FBX exports
* Added numbers and dash symbol to keyboard 🔢
* Autosave indicator (all of your latest changes are always saved)
* Fixed a bug where FBX exports were inside out in Unity 🐛
* Fixed a bug that happened when Poly models failed to download 🐛
* Other, minor bug fixes 🐛

notes.title: Major Release: 10X Performance & Camera
notes.content:
This is a major release that includes a more usable menu, a 4K Camera and a massive performance improvement 🔥

[h1] Performance now 10X Better [/h1]
We spent some time doing performance optimization for high-poly meshes and high-res textures. Now Sketchbox should run smoothly with meshes up to ~1M tris (used to be ~100K).
Great for 3D scans and photogrammetry. Even when you’re not using high-poly meshes, you’ll find save is now close to instant.


[h1] Share 4K images with Camera [/h1]
Many of you asked for an easier way to share Sketchbox projects to those without HMDs and now you can now save 4K images using the Camera. They are saved to C:\Users\<your-name>\Documents\Sketchbox\Screenshots.


[h1]Better Menu Design [/h1]
Our new menu is now much faster to use for novices and pros. Also — prettier. The controllers have also been updated so they’re more visible.


[h1] Much easier to use [/h1]
* Visual Guides for Snapping Lines
* The new guides make the line tool much easier to use. Part of our continued improvements to our grid and snapping system.

[h1] Other Improvements [/h1]
* We now support sub-folders for 3D Model imports 📂 — just drag and drop your folders to “/Sketchbox/Import/Mesh/”
* We now support transparent GLTFs, helpful for AR design
* Left-handed mode 👋
* Option to skip account creation (we heard you, Steam and Oculus reviewers 👌)
* We now officially support Windows 7️⃣& 8️⃣
* Minor Bug Fixes🐛

notes.title: Build Scenes Faster
notes.content:
[h1]Release: Build Scenes Faster[/h1]
Over the past two weeks we made building scenes faster, added a home area and added support for SketchFab models via glTF.


[h1]Models now Have ‘Snapping’[/h1]
At the beginning of January we added primitives and Poly so it was really easy to build a scene with models. Getting those models exactly how you wanted — like getting a plate to sit flat on a table — was tricky.

So I’m excited to announce that all models in Sketchbox now have snapping. It’s makes building scenes waaay faster. Models will now snap to the ground plane — so it’s easy to anchor and align objects. Models will also snap to each other, so you can build a house with primitives and get the rug and the dining room table to snap to the floor.

Snapping is difficult to get just right, and this is the first iteration — expect updates in February.


[h1]Support for glTF Import[/h1]
glTF is (hopefully) going to be the JPEG of 3D and we’re excited to announce that you can now import glTFs into Sketchbox.

Sketchfab is arguably the largest library of quality 3D assets and now all Sketchfab models that can be downloaded, can be used in Sketchbox as glTFs!

Learn how to import 3D models into Sketchbox here.


[h1]Find Examples in the Home Area[/h1]
You can now access example scenes from the home area, and load your saved sketches.


[h1]Tutorial… Now with Confetti![/h1]
As more and more people use Sketchbox, some of them who are new to VR, we knew it was time to improve our tutorial. And of course, there’s now confetti.

notes.title: Release: Find the Models you Need
notes.content:
This week we focused on 3D models.We made it easier to find models and if your search fails, build your own model with primitives.

[h1]Find the models you want with Poly[/h1]
You can now search Poly for exactly the model you want using a keyboard built into Sketchbox. Creating a scene has never been faster.

[h1]Create with Primitives[/h1]
Our most requested feature of all time is finally here! You can now add primitives directly from the menu and stretch them however you want. Primitives are especially useful if you’re building environments or you’re having trouble finding exactly the model you want.

[h1]Manipulate Models with Control Points[/h1]
All models in Sketchbox, including the models that you’ve imported can now be manipulated using control points that will be familiar to anyone that’s used a 3D modelling tool before. All models can be stretched on their X, Y or Z axis which makes it really easy to create variants of the same model.

notes.title: Huge Release: Create VR Storyboards with Sketchbox
notes.content:
This release has been in the works for a long time and I think it’s the biggest update we’ve ever made to Sketchbox: Storyboards and Google Poly.

[b]VR Storyboards[/b] 
You can now link multiple Sketchbox scenes together like slides in a presentation. We’ve also added a Presentation Mode which makes it super easy to walk anyone through a user flow. Especially someone who’s not too familiar with VR, like a client. You can put them in headset and step them through one scene at at time. They don’t even need to use the controllers and can’t ‘make a mistake’. Storyboards are particularly useful for long user flows like those found in a VR training simulations.

VR storyboards will also be fantastic for the pre-production of VR films, and animation. They’re infinitely better than a 2D storyboard at communicating how a shot really looks and feels.

[b]Google Poly[/b] 
We’ve added support for [url=https://poly.google.com/search/snow%20man]Google Poly[/url] so you can now import thousands of free models like these from Google Poly directly into your project. Next week you’ll be able to search through Poly models while you’re still in VR.


[b]New Features[/b] 
[list]
[*] Added Scenes & Presentation Mode, which are great for VR training simulations, VR content pre-production and detailed user flows. [url=https://intercom.help/sketchbox/getting-started-with-sketchbox/using-scenes-storyboarding]Docs here[/url].
[*] Google Poly models can now be added to any scene (search is coming very soon)
[*] You caw now import Meshes with Materials! Instructions for importing assets [url=https://intercom.help/sketchbox/getting-started-with-sketchbox/essentials-importing-assets-saving-shortcuts-naming-files]here[/url]
[*] Scale indicator added (1.0 means you’re at human size) which makes it much easier to get the right sense of scale
Preloaded primitives and common UI icons to make creating UI elements quicker
[*] The left hand palette is now always visible and the laser pointer is much easier to see
[*] The palette's design has been updated so that it’s easier to use
[*] With a new floor, it’s now easier to create large scenes
[*] Improved performance rendering
[/list]

Most of our new features come from your suggestions, so tell us what you want to see in Sketchbox by requesting a feature or emailing us.

notes.title: Sketchbox Release 8.22.2017: Rotate, and move through your scene! (and more!)
notes.content:
This week we added some of our most requested features, see below for changelog and please visit https://www.sketchboxvr.com/feedback to request a feature, or vote on a feature request! We check often 😃

New Features:

* Scale, and rotate the scene by holding both grips
* Move yourself through a scene by holding the left, or right grip
* Undo & Redo are now bound to left thumbpad (vive)/thumbstick (rift) and right thumbpad (vive)/thumbstick (rift) respectively.
* Lighting and materials have been tweaked to improve overall feel & comfort (thanks for the suggestion Lesley!)

Bug Fixes:

* Fixed a bug that would cause arbitrary crashes when using images in the scene
* Fixed bug where changing tool during left hand select causes items to be permanently selected
* Fixed a crash when exporting empty lines
* Fixed a crash when group/ungrouping/copying in certain cases

notes.title: Update
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

It's been a while since we released a build and I feel like you need an update. Since April development has been erratic due to a few distractions:

[list]
[*] In April we exhibited at VRLA and it was fantastic. We received tons of in-person usability feedback and spoke to 100s of people about how they're using/building/designing VR, all of which is helping us decide where to go with the product.
[*] We've been investigating ways to make 3D drawing easier. As great as 3D drawing is today, it feels like the true potential hasn't been reached. Our eyes aren't very good depth sensors, and our arms are only good at drawing some curves smoothly. In VR we can bend space and control the entire visual feed - there must be a better way to match the drawing experience to our bodies. This could easily take up _all_ our time, but frankly your feedback from the real product is even more valuable, so we're prioritizing the most promising ideas and trying to get the good ones into the product ASAP.
[/list]

That said, we have built some new stuff, which will be released in the next few weeks:

[list]
[*] dark/light mode
[*] increased contrast in lots of places and generally tweaked colors to make things more visible
[*] lots of changes to the selection/erase UI
[*] when you draw on a plane you should be able to revisit it, perhaps move the plane around, like you would a piece of paper. Haven't settled on a UI yet but we're getting there!
[/list]

Thanks to everyone who's using the tool, and please if you have any feedback jump on the forum or get us on team@sketchboxvr.com - we love it.

Cheers

notes.content:
Hi everyone,

It's been a while since we released a build and I feel like you need an update. Since April development has been erratic due to a few distractions:

[list]
[*] In April we exhibited at VRLA and it was fantastic. We received tons of in-person usability feedback and spoke to 100s of people about how they're using/building/designing VR, all of which is helping us decide where to go with the product.
[*] We've been investigating ways to make 3D drawing easier. As great as 3D drawing is today, it feels like the true potential hasn't been reached. Our eyes aren't very good depth sensors, and our arms are only good at drawing some curves smoothly. In VR we can bend space and control the entire visual feed - there must be a better way to match the drawing experience to our bodies. This could easily take up _all_ our time, but frankly your feedback from the real product is even more valuable, so we're prioritizing the most promising ideas and trying to get the good ones into the product ASAP.
[/list]

That said, we have built some new stuff, which will be released in the next few weeks:

[list]
[*] dark/light mode
[*] increased contrast in lots of places and generally tweaked colors to make things more visible
[*] lots of changes to the selection/erase UI
[*] when you draw on a plane you should be able to revisit it, perhaps move the plane around, like you would a piece of paper. Haven't settled on a UI yet but we're getting there!
[/list]

Thanks to everyone who's using the tool, and please if you have any feedback jump on the forum or get us on team@sketchboxvr.com - we love it.

Cheers
